title: Ancient Grain Explorer
task: Choose and try an ancient grain you have never tried before.
whyItMatters: Ancient grains contribute to dietary and agricultural diversity.

title: Create a Sustainable Menu
task: Design a full day's menu including: one pulse, one alternative staple food and not more than one meal containing meat.
whyItMatters: Meal planning helps translate knowledge into behaviour.

title: Share a Sustainable Recipe
task: Choose a sustainable recipe and share it with someone
whyItMatters: Food habits are influenced by social environments.

title: Food System Detective
task: Explore food facts and try to understand how do pulses help improve soil fertility
whyItMatters: Understanding food production helps support sustainable choices.

title: Environmental Impact Expert
task: Discover the environmental impacts of: beef, pork, chicken and legumes. Rank them from highest impact to lowest impact
whyItMatters: Comparing foods can reveal large differences in environmental impacts.

title: Build a Sustainable Shopping Basket
task: Create a hypothetical shopping basket containing: one seasonal product; one local product; one certified product and one lower-carbon protein source.
whyItMatters: Sustainable food choices involve multiple considerations beyond nutrition.

title: Land Use Expert
task: Review four foods and try to collect information to rank them according to how much agricultural land they require.
whyItMatters: Food choices strongly influence global land use.Roughly half of the world's habitable land is used for agriculture.

title: Water Footprint Investigator
task: Choose one food you eat regularly and investigate whether its production is likely associated with high or low water use.
whyItMatters: Different foods place very different pressures on freshwater resources. The water footprint of a diet depends heavily on what people eat.

title: Sustainability Label Comparison
task: Compare two sustainability certifications found on food products and identify: what they certify; what information they provide and what differences exist between them
whyItMatters: Different certifications address different sustainability issues.

title: Product Impact Reflection
task: Choose one product you regularly purchase and reflect on three environmental dimensions that might influence its sustainability: land use, water use, carbon footprint, transport distance and production method.
whyItMatters: Sustainability is multidimensional and cannot be determined by a single indicator.

title: The Limits of a Single Score
task: Choose a product and evaluate why one indicator alone is enough to understand its sustainability and quality. Use Nutri-Score, NOVA classification, Green-Score and ingredient-list information when available.
whyItMatters: No single metric captures every dimension of food sustainability.

title: The NOVA Debate
task: Choose one product and consider whether its NOVA classification seems intuitive based on the ingredient list and product description. Use NOVA information and packaging details.
whyItMatters: The NOVA framework remains widely discussed and debated within food science.

title: Food Processing Analysis
task: Choose a processed food and analyse how processing might influence convenience, shelf life, nutrition and environmental impacts.
whyItMatters: The impacts of processing extend beyond a single outcome.

title: Indicator Conflict Explorer
task: Find a product with a relatively good performance on one indicator and a relatively poor performance on another. Try to understand why this might occur.Use Green-Score, NOVA classification, Nutri-Score and Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Different indicators are designed to answer different questions.

title: Which Indicator Do You Trust Most?
task: Compare several products and reflect on which indicator you personally find most useful when choosing foods and why. Use packaging, Open Food Facts, Nutri-Score, NOVA classification and Green-Score.
whyItMatters: Consumers increasingly face multiple indicators and must decide how to use them.

title: The Packaging Dilemma
task: Find a product with extensive packaging and discuss whether the additional packaging might be justified.
whyItMatters: Packaging should minimise material use without compromising food safety or increasing food waste.

title: Which Is More Sustainable?
task: Compare two packaging materials used for the same type of food and think if identifying a single "best" option is possible.
whyItMatters: No packaging material is universally the most sustainable option across all situations.

title: Circular Economy Reflection
task: Choose one food package and analyse how it could move through a circular economy system after use.
whyItMatters: Circular economy approaches aim to keep materials in use through reuse and recycling.

title: Future Packaging Explorer
task: Investigate one packaging innovation such as edible packaging, active packaging or intelligent packaging and reflect on the problem it attempts to solve.
whyItMatters: Edible, active and intelligent packaging systems have the potential to reduce waste and improve food preservation.

title: One Product, Multiple Perspectives
task: Evaluate one food package from three perspectives: resource use, food protection and end-of-life management. Reflect on which perspective you consider most important and why.
whyItMatters: Packaging sustainability cannot be determined by a single characteristic, but depends on the balance between protection, resource use and circularity.

title: Leftover Transformation
task: Use at least one leftover ingredient or leftover meal to create a new meal or snack.
whyItMatters: Reusing leftovers is one of the most effective ways to prevent edible food from becoming waste.

title: The Empty Fridge Test
task: Open your fridge and identify one food that should be eaten within the next two days. Make a plan to make sure it is not wasted.
whyItMatters: Many foods become waste simply because they are overlooked.

title: One Change, Biggest Impact
task: Pick one food-waste habit that you would realistically be willing to change this month.
whyItMatters: Sustainable behaviour change often starts with one achievable action.

title: Eat Me First Zone
task: Create an "Eat Me First" area in your fridge, freezer or pantry and place all foods that should be consumed soon in that location.
whyItMatters: Foods that are visible are less likely to be forgotten and wasted.

title: Shelf-Life Rescue
task: Choose three foods in your kitchen with the shortest remaining shelf life and move them to a visible location.
whyItMatters: Many foods become waste because they are forgotten behind newer products.

title: Sodium Hotspot
task: Identify the food in your kitchen with the highest salt content per 100 grams.
whyItMatters: Most sodium comes from processed foods rather than table salt.

title: Hidden Sugar Hunt
task: Identify the food in your home with the highest sugar content per 100 grams.
whyItMatters: Large amounts of sugar can be present in unexpected foods.

title: Nutrient Density Check
task: Choose a food you consume regularly and identify whether its main contribution is protein, fibre, vitamins, healthy fats, or mostly calories.
whyItMatters: Not all foods contribute equally to nutritional quality.

title: Rainbow Audit
task: Review yesterday's meals and count how many different fruit and vegetable colours you consumed.
whyItMatters: Dietary diversity supports micronutrient intake.

title: Micronutrient Source Hunt
task: Find one food in your kitchen that is a good source of vitamin C, one that provides vitamin A, and one that contributes vitamin E or vitamin B12.
whyItMatters: Many people understand macronutrients but struggle to identify sources of essential vitamins.

title: Which Protein Has the Lowest Footprint?
task: Go to the shopping list and compare the footprint of two proteins that you consume often
whyItMatters: Different protein sources have very different environmental impacts.

title: Find Three Non-Meat Proteins
task: Open your fridge, pantry, or food cupboard and identify three foods that contain protein but are not meat.
whyItMatters: Protein comes from many foods besides meat.

title: Discover Lentils
task: Explore food facts and identify two nutritional or environmental benefits of lentils.
whyItMatters: Lentils are nutritious and environmentally friendly.

title: Spot the Hidden Meat
task: Think about everything you ate yesterday and identify foods that contained processed meat.
whyItMatters: Processed meat can be present in many everyday foods.

title: Build Your Sustainable Food Wishlist
task: One meat-free recipe you would like to taste.
whyItMatters: Trying new foods can help diversify diets.

title: Label Explorer
task: Pick one packaged food product and identify the following information on the label: country of origin; ingredient list and nutrition information
whyItMatters: Food labels contain valuable information that can help consumers better understand food products and make informed choices.Food origin can provide useful information about traceability and sustainability.

title: Country Detective
task: Look at three food products in your kitchen and identify where they were produced.
whyItMatters: Food often travels long distances before reaching consumers.Global food transport generates approximately 3 billion tonnes of CO₂-equivalent emissions annually.

title: Find a Seasonal Food
task: Identify one fruit or vegetable currently in season in your region and locate it in a shop or market.
whyItMatters: Seasonal foods may require less storage and transportation.Choosing seasonal foods can help reduce food-related emissions.

title: Spot the Certification
task: Find a food product carrying a sustainability-related certification or label.Examples: organic, fairtrade or protected designation of origin.
whyItMatters: Labels can provide information about how food is produced.

title: Packaging Journey
task: Choose one packaged food product from your kitchen and investigate: where it was produced, where it was packaged (if available) and one ingredient that comes from another country.
whyItMatters: Many food products involve global supply chains before reaching consumers.

title: Decoding the Ingredient List
task: Choose a packaged food and read its ingredient list from start to finish. Identify three ingredients you recognize and one ingredient you do not recognize.
whyItMatters: Ingredient lists can reveal how foods are formulated and processed.

title: What Does NOVA Measure?
task: Choose one food product and investigate why it belongs to its NOVA category. Use Open Food Facts and compare the NOVA classification with the ingredient list.
whyItMatters: Processing is not always obvious from appearance alone.

title: Packaging Clue Hunt
task: Choose one packaged food and identify all the information on the package that provides clues about how it was produced or processed.
whyItMatters: Many consumers overlook information that is already available on food packaging.

title: One Food, Many Steps
task: Pick one food product and explore of what may have happened between the raw ingredients and the final product you purchased.
whyItMatters: Food processing often involves multiple transformation steps that consumers never see.

title: Three Labels, Three Stories
task: Find a product displaying at least two of the following indicators: Nutri-Score, NOVA classification or Green-Score. Understand what each indicator is trying to measure.
whyItMatters: Different labels communicate different kinds of information.

title: The Packaging Guessing Game
task: Choose a food product and imagine it was sold without its current packaging. What problems might occur before it reaches your home?
whyItMatters: Many consumers see packaging only as waste and overlook its role in food protection.

title: Spot the Packaging Function
task: Choose one food package and identify the main function it serves. Is it primarily protecting the food, extending shelf life, providing information, enabling transport, or allowing reuse?
whyItMatters: Packaging often serves several functions simultaneously.

title: Can You Recycle It?
task: Choose one package and make your best guess about how it should be disposed of before reading the disposal instructions. Then compare your answer with the actual label.
whyItMatters: Consumers often misunderstand packaging disposal rules.Correct sorting improves recycling efficiency and material recovery.

title: Packaging Myth Buster
task: Ask yourself whether less packaging is always more sustainable. Use one food product as an example.
whyItMatters: Packaging reduction is not always environmentally beneficial.Packaging that prevents food spoilage can sometimes provide greater environmental benefits than eliminating packaging altogether.

title: Before Throwing It Away
task: Before disposing of one food package, think of at least one way it could be reused.
whyItMatters: Reuse extends the useful life of materials. Reuse systems keep materials in circulation longer and reduce the demand for virgin resources.

title: Best Before or Use By?
task: Choose five food products in your kitchen and identify whether they display a best-before date or a use-by date. Understand the difference between the two.
whyItMatters: Many consumers confuse date labels and discard edible food unnecessarily.

title: The Forgotten Food Hunt
task: Find the oldest edible food product currently stored in your fridge, freezer, or pantry.
whyItMatters: Food that is forgotten is much more likely to become waste.

title: Food Waste Snapshot
task: Think about the last three foods you discarded.
whyItMatters: Understanding your own waste patterns is the first step toward reducing them.

title: Portion Prediction Test
task: Before a meal, estimate how much food you think you will eat.After the meal, compare your estimate with what you actually consumed.
whyItMatters: People often overestimate their hunger.

title: The Cost of Waste
task: Estimate the financial value of the last edible food item that was discarded in your household.
whyItMatters: Food waste affects household budgets as well as the environment.

title: Find the Protein Source
task: Find the packaged food in your kitchen that contains the most protein per 100 grams.
whyItMatters: Protein content varies considerably across foods.

title: Sugar Detective
task: Compare two packaged foods and determine which contains more sugar per 100 grams.
whyItMatters: Foods that appear similar often have very different sugar contents.

title: Fibre Finder
task: Find three foods in your kitchen that naturally contain fibre.
whyItMatters: Fibre is found almost exclusively in plant foods.

title: Salt Spotter
task: Choose one packaged food and determine how much salt it contains per 100 grams.
whyItMatters: Many foods contain hidden sodium.

title: Protein Claim Explorer
task: Find a product carrying a protein claim and determine whether it qualifies as a source of protein or a high-protein food.
whyItMatters: Nutrition claims follow specific criteria.

title: Try a New Pulse
task: Choose one pulse you rarely or never eat.Taste it for the first time or prepare it in a new way.
whyItMatters: Pulses are among the most sustainable protein-rich foods available.

title: Protein Comparison
task: Read the labels of two products that you have at home and compare the amount of protein they contain
whyItMatters: Understanding impacts helps support informed choices.

title: Discover Quinoa
task: Explore food facts and discover why quinoa is considered a "complete protein".
whyItMatters: Quinoa offers nutritional diversity.

title: Sustainable Shopping Scan
task: During your next shopping trip, identify one alternative grain
whyItMatters: Food choices begin before consumption.

title: Recipe Explorer
task: Search the recipe library and find one recipe that could replace a regular meat-based meal you eat.
whyItMatters: Cooking skills facilitate dietary change.

title: Food Miles Investigator
task: Select one food product and estimate how far it travelled before reaching your table using the country of origin shown on the packaging.
whyItMatters: Transport contributes to the environmental footprint of food.

title: Production Method Hunt
task: Find two products produced using different farming methods.Examples: organic vs conventional; greenhouse-grown vs field-grown
whyItMatters: How food is produced can be as important as what food is produced.

title: Local vs Imported
task: Compare a local product and an imported product in the same food category. Identify: country of origin and production method.
whyItMatters: Country of origin alone does not determine sustainability.How food is produced often matters more than the distance it travels.

title: Environmental Claim Detective
task: Find a product making an environmental claim (e.g. carbon neutral; sustainable; eco-friendly; planet-friendly. Identify other information in the label provided to support the claim.
whyItMatters: Understanding sustainability claims helps consumers make informed decisions.

title: Supermarket Land-Use Explorer
task: During your next shopping trip, identify: one beef product; one poultry product and one plant-based protein product. Take a photo or make a note of the products and reflect on which one you think required the most agricultural land to produce.
whyItMatters: Different foods require vastly different amounts of land, even when they provide similar nutrients.

title: The Processing Spectrum
task: Find three foods that appear to represent different levels of processing and understand why. Use ingredient lists and NOVA classifications.
whyItMatters: Foods exist on a spectrum rather than being simply processed or unprocessed.

title: Processing Benefit, Processing Cost
task: Choose one processed food and identify one advantage and one potential drawback of the processing used to produce it. Use packaging, ingredient lists and Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Food processing can improve preservation and safety while increasing energy and resource use.

title: When Scores Disagree
task: Find a food product for which two indicators provide different signals. For example, a favourable Nutri-Score but a high NOVA classification. Use packaging or Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Nutritional quality, affordability and degree of processing do not always align.

title: Food Technology Explorer
task: Find a product that uses a production or formulation technology you were previously unfamiliar with and learn what it does. Use ingredient lists, packaging descriptions or Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Modern food systems depend on many technologies that consumers rarely notice.

title: Product Reformulation Detective
task: Compare two similar products and investigate why one has a better Nutri-Score or Green-Score than the other.
whyItMatters: Small formulation changes can influence food ratings.

title: Food Waste Versus Packaging Waste
task: Choose a highly perishable food and reflect on what would happen if its packaging provided less protection.
whyItMatters: Packaging can reduce food loss and waste by extending shelf life and protecting food quality.

title: The Reuse Break-Even Challenge
task: Choose a reusable container you own and estimate how many times you think it would need to be reused before becoming environmentally preferable to a disposable version.
whyItMatters: Reuse requires repeated use to generate benefits. Reusable packaging becomes environmentally beneficial only after reaching a reuse break-even point.

title: Why Do Similar Foods Have Different Packaging?
task: Compare two similar foods sold in different packaging formats and think about why manufacturers may have chosen different solutions.
whyItMatters: The most sustainable packaging depends on the food product, shelf life requirements and supply chain conditions.

title: Smart Packaging Explorer
task: Find a package that includes a freshness indicator, temperature indicator or traceability feature and investigate what problem it is designed to solve.
whyItMatters: Packaging is increasingly used to communicate information and reduce waste. Intelligent packaging can monitor or communicate information about food quality and condition.

title: The Most Important Packaging Feature
task: Choose one food product and decide which packaging function is most important for that product: protection, information, convenience, shelf-life extension, recyclability or reuse.
whyItMatters: Packaging must balance food safety, preservation and environmental performance.

title: Food Waste Detective
task: Identify the single biggest reason food is wasted in your household.
whyItMatters: Different causes require different solutions.

title: Promotion Trap Check
task: Think about a recent "buy one get one free", multipack, or bulk purchase.
whyItMatters: Special offers can sometimes encourage consumers to buy more than they need.

title: High-Impact Waste Reflection
task: Look into the food facts to understand the difference of the environmental consequences of wasting: one serving of meat and one serving of lentils.
whyItMatters: Not all wasted foods have the same environmental footprint.

title: Food Waste Hotspots
task: Identify the three foods currently in your home that are most at risk of becoming waste within the next week.
whyItMatters: Recognising risk early can help prevent waste.

title: Why Did It Go Bad?
task: Think about the most recent food product you threw away and the cause.
whyItMatters: Food waste is often avoidable when underlying causes are identified.

title: Whole Grain Check
task: Examine the ingredient list of a whole grained labelled product and determine whether it is genuinely whole grain. A whole grain should be the first ingredient in the ingredient list.
whyItMatters: Packaging claims can be misleading.

title: Drink Comparison
task: Compare two sweet beverages that you enjoy drinking and identify which contains less sugar per 100 ml.
whyItMatters: Beverages are major sources of free sugars.

title: Fat Explorer
task: Find one food in your kitchen that is mainly a source of unsaturated fat and one that is mainly a source of saturated fat.
whyItMatters: Different fats influence health differently.

title: Fibre Ratio Test
task: Evaluate one grain product using the 10:1 carbohydrate-to-fibre rule. The rule states: For every 10 grams of carbohydrates, there should be at least 1 gram of fibre.
whyItMatters: This ratio can help identify healthier grain products.

title: Protein Package Challenge
task: Compare two protein-rich foods and assess what accompanies the protein, such as fibre, healthy fats, sodium or saturated fat.
whyItMatters: The overall nutritional package matters as much as the protein itself.
